topics.name: Financial accounting: the double-entry system and verification

questions.q: Which error causes the trial balance not to agree?
o: Transposition in one ledger account only
questions.why: A one-sided error makes total debits differ from total credits.

questions.q: A suspense account is opened when…
o: the trial balance does not agree
questions.why: The difference is held temporarily until errors are found and corrected.

questions.q: A sales ledger control account helps to…
o: check the accuracy of individual customer accounts
questions.why: Its balance should equal the total of the customer (trade receivables) accounts.

questions.q: 75 000 new $1 ordinary shares are issued at $3.50 each. How much is credited to share premium?
questions.why: Examiners (2023): the popular distractor used only part of the issue price. Separate nominal value (share capital) from premium: 75 000 × ($3.50 − $1.00) = $187 500.

questions.q: Opening trade receivables are $12 000. Credit sales are $80 000, receipts from credit customers $75 000, discounts allowed $1 500 and irrecoverable debts written off $500. What is the closing balance on the sales ledger control account?
questions.why: Closing balance = 12 000 + 80 000 − 75 000 − 1 500 − 500 = $15 000; discounts allowed and irrecoverable debts both reduce what customers owe.

topics.name: Financial accounting: adjustments and financial statements

questions.q: Inventory should be valued at…
o: the lower of cost and net realisable value
the higher of cost and NRV
questions.why: IAS 2 and the prudence principle.

questions.q: Reducing-balance depreciation charges…
o: more in early years, less later
questions.why: A fixed percentage is applied to the falling carrying value.

questions.q: Accrued expenses at year end are shown as…
questions.why: Money is owed for expenses already incurred.

questions.q: Which is the book of prime entry for writing off an irrecoverable debt?
questions.why: Examiners (2023): the most common error was to name the sales ledger rather than the journal.

questions.q: Goods taken by the owner for personal use are recorded as:
questions.why: Examiners (2023): some reversed the entries or used the wrong accounts.

long.q: A machine cost $50 000 and is depreciated at 20% a year using the reducing balance method. Calculate the depreciation for years 1 and 2 and the net book value at the end of year 2.
scheme: M1: net book value after year 1 = $40 000

long.q: Trade receivables are $40 000. The allowance for irrecoverable debts is to be 5% of trade receivables; last year's allowance was $1500. Calculate the entry in the income statement and the net figure shown in the statement of financial position.
scheme: A1: increase of $500 charged to the income statement

topics.name: Financial accounting: partnerships and limited companies

questions.q: If a partnership agreement is silent, profits are shared…
questions.why: Default rules apply when there is no agreement.

questions.q: Share premium arises when shares are issued…
questions.why: The excess over nominal value goes to the share premium account.

questions.q: With no partnership agreement, how are profits shared under the Partnership Act 1890?
o: Equally, with no interest on capital or salaries
questions.why: Interest on loans from partners is 5% a year.

questions.q: X and Y share residual profits 3 : 2. Profit for the year is $50 000. Interest on capital is X $3 000 and Y $2 000, and Y receives a salary of $5 000. What is X's share of the residual profit?
questions.why: Residual profit = 50 000 − 5 000 interest − 5 000 salary = $40 000, and X receives 3/5 of it = $24 000.

questions.q: A company with 200 000 ordinary shares of $1 makes a 1 for 4 bonus issue, financed from share premium. What is the effect?
o: Share capital rises by $50 000 and share premium falls by $50 000
Cash rises by $50 000 and share capital rises by $50 000
Share capital rises by $200 000 and retained earnings fall by $200 000
questions.why: 50 000 new shares are issued free, so a reserve is converted into share capital; no cash is received and total equity is unchanged.

long.q: A and B are partners. A's capital is $50 000 and B's $30 000. Interest on capital is 5%, B receives a salary of $10 000, and remaining profits are shared 3 : 2. Profit for the year is $60 000. Prepare the figures for the appropriation account.
scheme: M1: interest on capital: A $2500, B $1500

questions.q: Trade receivables turnover in days is…
questions.why: It shows how long customers take to pay.

questions.q: Gearing measures…
o: the proportion of capital financed by long-term debt
questions.why: Highly geared businesses carry more financial risk.

questions.q: Which ratio shows how many days customers take to pay?
questions.why: Trade receivables ÷ credit sales × 365.

questions.q: A business has current assets of $45 000, including inventory of $18 000, and current liabilities of $30 000. What is its liquid (acid test) ratio?
questions.why: Liquid ratio = (current assets − inventory) ÷ current liabilities = 27 000 ÷ 30 000 = 0.9 : 1.

questions.q: Profit from operations is $36 000. Equity is $150 000 and non-current liabilities are $50 000. What is the return on capital employed?
questions.why: Capital employed = equity + non-current liabilities = $200 000, so ROCE = 36 000 ÷ 200 000 × 100 = 18%.

long.q: A business has revenue of $200 000 and cost of sales of $140 000. Calculate its gross margin and its mark-up.

questions.q: Contribution per unit is…
o: selling price − fixed cost per unit
selling price − variable cost per unit
questions.why: Contribution covers fixed costs, then gives profit.

questions.q: In absorption costing, overheads are absorbed using…
questions.why: For example, per direct labour hour or machine hour.

questions.q: Break-even output is 1 250.4 units. What should be stated?
questions.why: Examiners (2023): the break-even point was often not rounded up to the nearest whole unit.

questions.q: Marginal cost is:
o: The extra cost of producing one more unit
questions.why: Examiners (2023): few defined it correctly, often leaving out 'one additional unit'.

questions.q: Budgeted overheads are $120 000 and budgeted direct labour hours are 40 000. Overheads are absorbed on a labour-hour basis. How much overhead is absorbed by a job taking 25 labour hours?
questions.why: The absorption rate is 120 000 ÷ 40 000 = $3 per labour hour, so the job absorbs 25 × 3 = $75.

long.q: A firm with spare capacity is offered a one-off order for 500 units at $15 each. The variable cost is $11 a unit and fixed costs are already covered. Advise whether to accept, with one non-financial factor.
scheme: A1: total contribution = 500 × 4 = $2000, so profit rises: accept
B1: one non-financial factor, e.g. regular customers may ask for the same low price
B1: or the order may lead to future business / uses idle staff

questions.q: A statement of cash flows classifies cash flows under…
questions.why: IAS 7 uses these three headings.

questions.q: Goodwill arises when…
o: a business is bought for more than the fair value of its net assets
questions.why: It reflects reputation, customers and other unrecorded value.

questions.q: In a business combination, goodwill is:
o: The book value of the assets
The price paid above the fair value of the net assets acquired
questions.why: It is an intangible non-current asset.

questions.q: Using the indirect method, how is an increase in trade receivables of $4 000 treated when calculating cash flow from operating activities?
o: Ignored, as it is not a cash item
questions.why: More sales are tied up in amounts not yet received, so less cash has come in than the profit suggests; the increase is deducted.

questions.q: A company revalues its land from $200 000 to $260 000. Where is the $60 000 gain recorded?
o: As revenue in the income statement
questions.why: An unrealised revaluation gain is not trading profit, so it is credited to a revaluation reserve within equity (through other comprehensive income).

long.q: Explain two limitations of using ratio analysis to compare two companies.
scheme: B1: different accounting policies (e.g. depreciation) distort comparisons
B1: historical data may not reflect the future / window dressing

questions.q: A favourable materials price variance means…
questions.why: Actual price below standard price saves money.

questions.q: A project's NPV is positive. This means…
o: it earns more than the cost of capital
it pays back in one year
questions.why: Discounted inflows exceed outflows at the chosen rate.

questions.q: Which method uses the net present value of future cash flows?
questions.why: Examiners (2023): ARR uses the average investment, not the total.

questions.q: The standard labour rate is $12 an hour. Workers were paid $25 000 for 2 000 hours. What is the labour rate variance?
questions.why: Standard cost of the actual hours = 2 000 × 12 = $24 000; actual pay of $25 000 is $1 000 more, so the variance is adverse.

questions.q: A project costs $20 000 now and returns $12 000 at the end of each of years 1 and 2. Discount factors at 10% are 0.909 and 0.826. What is the net present value?

long.q: A product has a standard of 2 kg of material at $5 per kg. 1000 units used 2100 kg costing $10 080. Calculate the material price and usage variances.
